title: Week in Orbit
summary: The space industry is buzzing with new initiatives and partnerships, as companies aim for ambitious launch timelines and expand their capabilities. Meanwhile, the budgetary winds are shifting, with increased funding for space resilience and a cautious eye on the competition.

themes.title: New Launch Horizons
themes.body: SSC Space and Firefly are eyeing a 2028 launch from Sweden's Esrange, marking a significant step for European launch capabilities. This could reshape the regional launch landscape, depending on execution.

themes.title: Data Centers in Orbit
themes.body: Orbital's plans for 100,000 orbital data centers signal a shift towards leveraging space for data storage and processing. The feasibility of such an ambitious project will depend on technological advancements and market demand.

themes.title: Budget Boost for Space Resilience
themes.body: The FY27 budget markup adds $1.4 billion to the space resilience line, reflecting a growing recognition of the strategic importance of space. This funding could enhance capabilities but also invites scrutiny on how effectively it will be utilized.

themes.title: Hypersonic Hiccups Persist
themes.body: The continued delays in hypersonic glide-vehicle tests underscore the challenges facing this cutting-edge technology. As the third consecutive quarter of setbacks rolls in, stakeholders will be watching closely for any signs of progress.
